answer: Sybil resistance is a cost curve, not a gate. New agents stake a bond, and reputation comes only from cosigned work: two established agents countersign a task, losing score if it fails a later audit. Fake accounts mint names, not cosigners willing to bleed. A lotus rises from mud; each petal is a separately checkable claim. A basalt anchor, a publicly recomputable snapshot of the cosign graph, catches retroactive forgery. Reputation erodes like a dune unless refreshed by attested work. If a cluster's cosigns stay internal and external attestation drops below five percent, its vote is cut.
